messages:
maria_support: FYI we've got an escalation from ACME — sustained p95/p99 latency from EU callers, intermittent 503/401s. customer sees requests suddenly routed to US with huge tail latency. attaching snippets below.
acme_infra: yep, started ~11:02Z. traffic to eu-west saturated then latency jumped to 2.5s p95 and some requests failed with 401s. no config changes on our side. :frown:
maria_support: request ids — 8a3f2b, 8a3f2c. full logs pasted.
kevin_sre: looking at infra: eu-west pool hit queue depth threshold at 11:03:12Z. Router engaged fallback policy and started proxying to fallback region (us-west) instead of returning a redirect. ops-bot alert: "region_capacity: eu-west active_queues=1248 threshold=1000"
linh_eng: interesting — was fallback set to transparent proxy or redirect? we have two modes.
kevin_sre: configured as "drain + transparent" by default for safety, so requests are forwarded to fallback. that avoids 5xx for callers but can create cross-region auth semantics issues.
acme_infra: we observed that some calls proxied to us-west returned 401 with token_audience mismatch. our tokens are short-lived and scoped to eu audience.
linh_eng: aha — transparent proxy keeps original Authorization header. if token audience is region-scoped, the target region will reject. can reproduce locally if we saturate eu pool.
maria_support: can you paste a repro curl? customer asked for reproducible steps.
linh_eng: repro:
```
# create burst to saturate local pool then hit generate
for i in {1..1200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $EU_TOKEN" -H "X-Region-Hint: eu-west" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate >/dev/null & done
```
Then you'll see a mixture of slow 200s from us-west and 401s.
kevin_sre: root cause summary: when eu pool reaches drain threshold the router transparently proxies to fallback. transparent proxy preserves original token -> audience mismatch -> 401s. additionally, because requests hit fallback region, egress/replication costs spike (customer billing alert).
maria_support: customer is upset about both latency and surprise billing. what immediate mitigations?
kevin_sre: options: 1) temporarily pin their org to eu-west (quickest) 2) change fallback to 307 redirect so clients can choose new token 3) implement token-exchange in router (longer-term) 4) increase eu capacity (expensive)
linh_eng: also can shorten drain window so routers fail faster to avoid cross-region amplification. current drain window was 5m; lowering to 30s reduces silent proxy period.
acme_infra: we'll take pin for now. please confirm steps and expected downtime.
maria_support: applying manual pin now, will update.
deploy-bot: action: apply_route_pin org=acme id=acme-123 region=eu-west ttl=2h — started at 11:25:43Z
maria_support: pin applied. ask customer to validate.
acme_infra: traffic looks back to eu-west, p95 improved. thanks. billing team still flagged inter-region egress from the 11:03–11:25 window.
kevin_sre: follow ups: open PR to add audience-exchange in router (linh), add explicit header X-Fallback-Mode returned to client, update runbook to prefer redirect for region-scoped tokens, and lower default drain window.
linh_eng: filed PR #2145 to implement token-exchange + tests.
kevin_sre: we'll also add an observability metric "fallback_type" and alert when transparent_fallback_count > 10/m.
ops-bot: incident note created: INC-2026 region silent-fallback caused auth mismatch + billing spike. severity: P2.
kevin_sre: schedule postmortem and coordinate with pricing team for customer billing review.
maria_support: I'll draft the customer summary and next steps (pin applied, engineering fixes planned, billing review). tagging for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
